title: 2027-02-28-meridiangrid-security-playbook-and-deployment-paths-discovery
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment
summary: Initial security posture discovery for MeridianGrid Utilities evaluating Redwood's hosting options. Main concerns: KMS/HSM integration, SSO and SCIM provisioning, audit log retention & access, SOC2/ISO evidence, and precise RBAC controls. Team requested SOC2 cert, network diagram, and a small pilot checklist + pricing cadence for Dedicated/Private.
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 report and security whitepaper (Claire)
SE to run suggested pilot checklist and sample infra diagram (Ravi)
Customer to send current SSO IdP metadata and compliance calendar (Ellen)
action_items: Claire Soto - send SOC2 attestation + security whitepaper - due 2027-03-02
Ravi Patel - provide sample Private deployment network diagram and KMS integration notes - due 2027-03-04
Ellen Park - share SAML metadata and current RBAC policy export - due 2027-03-03
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Claire Soto (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Ellen Park (CISO, MeridianGrid), Marcus Li (Platform), Tara Gomez (Compliance), Ben Ortiz (CTO)

Optional sections: Summary / Topics / Action items included above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Claire Soto: hi everyone, thank you for joining, this is Claire from Redwood Inference, and with me is Ravi, our solution engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Ellen Park: doing well, thanks. we've got about 50 minutes, want to focus on security posture and the hosting options. we've been asked to validate if Redwood can meet our controls for utilities data, so, social two, sorry SOC2, SAML, audit log retention, KMS and data residency.
[00:22] Claire Soto: absolutely, that's what we wanted to cover. quick intro from you folks to set context? who's driving the compliance checklist?
[00:27] Marcus Li: i'm Marcus, platform eng, i'll be doing the integration. ben's our CTO and tara's on compliance so she'll sign off. our timeline is about Q2 pilot then production by late Q3, if everything looks good.
[00:38] Tara Gomez: yeah, we need the SOC2 type II report, plus ISO27001 evidence would be great. also curious about log retention and access controls. we have a two year retention policy for some telemetry.
[00:48] Ravi Patel: quick note, Redwood has SOC2 and we publish certs, i'll share the exact reports after. our platform supports hosted, dedicated and private deployments — we can map controls differently depending on where you land.
[00:58] Ben Ortiz: big item for us is KMS integration. we use cloud KMS with envelope encryption and an on-prem HSM for highest sens data. can Redwood integrate with customer-managed KMS or HSM?
[01:12] Claire Soto: yes, for Private we offer customer-managed key integration and can work with customer KMS providers. for Dedicated we have a bring-your-own-key option via our KMS bridge; hosted has envelope/e2e options with Redwood KMS or customer KMS in supported clouds. i'll let Ravi expand.
[01:26] Ravi Patel: right, technical detail — we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault for key wrapping. we also support HSM-backed keys via KMIP or cloud HSM when deployed in Private. there are two common patterns: keys stored in your KMS, we do envelope encryption for model artifacts and token payloads; or in Private mode you can deploy a local HSM and we route signing calls over mTLS to your HSM gateway.
[01:49] Tara Gomez: ok, and how are logs handled? we need audit trails for both admin actions and per-request metadata. retention windows need to be configurable per-tenant.
[01:59] Ravi Patel: audit logs are captured at the request, model and infra layers. admin events go into an audit log store, and we can ship logs to your SIEM via syslog/HTTP(s) or S3. retention can be configured — hosted defaults to 90 days, we can extend for Dedicated or Private via contractual add-on. note: some of the older infra exports have slightly different field names, so there may be mapping needed.
[02:21] Marcus Li: is there RBAC for token-level controls? we want least privilege so feature teams only can call certain model endpoints and not access customer keys.
[02:31] Claire Soto: yes, we expose RBAC with roles: admin, ops, dev, read-only, plus custom roles. policy enforcement is integrated into the Console and via API tokens. we also support SCIM for provisioning and SAML 2.0 for SSO.
[02:43] Ellen Park: on SSO and SCIM — we use Okta and Azure AD. we want just-in-time provisioning and SAML assertions mapped to roles. is SCIM available for user lifecycle?
[02:53] Ravi Patel: SCIM is supported for Dedicated and Private right now; hosted plans can enable it with enterprise tier. SAML attributes can be mapped to roles. there may be a couple of small claims mapping steps depending on your IdP.
[03:07] Tara Gomez: compliance question — do you provide immutable tamper-proof logs? our internal auditors want write-once storage for critical events.
[03:16] Ravi Patel: for Dedicated/Private we can configure WORM on the storage buckets or push to your WORM-compliant archive. hosted logs are in append-only stores but if you need certified WORM we recommend Private or dedicated archival to your tenant-controlled storage.
[03:30] Ben Ortiz: network segmentation — if we go Private on prem, can we run the control plane in our VPC entirely? we want no egress to public internet for model payloads.
[03:41] Claire Soto: Private lets you host the inference runtime in your VPC or on-prem. the control plane optionally remains managed by Redwood but can be run in a customer-proxied mode where API calls route through your network. fully air-gapped deployments are supported under our on-prem package but require additional ops work and lead time.
[03:58] Marcus Li: vendor lock-in question — we run some LLMs in house and want to fall back to our own endpoints if Redwood has an outage. is there native routing / failover?
[04:08] Ravi Patel: we have smart routing and fallback policies; you can configure a routing policy to send to a secondary endpoint which could be your in-house model. latency and tokenization differences are caveats.
[04:20] Ellen Park: any third-party pen test reports or on-demand pentests? we do yearly third-party assessments and need to know if Redwood participates.
[04:30] Claire Soto: we run annual pen tests and can share summary results; full reports require NDA. we also use 3rd-party continuous scanning tools and maintain a vulnerability disclosure program.
[04:40] Tara Gomez: retention specifics — we have PII in prompts occasionally; do you support redaction or automated PII scrubbing before logs are persisted?
[04:50] Ravi Patel: there are two controls: client-side scrubbing via a pre-send filter (we have SDK hooks) and server-side redaction rules that can mask fields in logs before storage. for strict PII avoidance we recommend client-side filters and private deployment with no persistent prompt logs.
[05:06] Ben Ortiz: curious about model caching and kv cache — if we keep KV cache in memory, is that encrypted at rest? and who has access to keys?
[05:18] Ravi Patel: KV cache is in-memory by default; snapshots may be written to disk for warm restarts. disk snapshots are encrypted using the same envelope key approach and are tenant-scoped. access is restricted to the runtime service account, and KMS controls key access. for Dedicated/Private you control the master key.
[05:36] Marcus Li: endpoint-level metrics — who can see token-level telemetry? we need to limit to SRE and compliance only.
[05:44] Claire Soto: Console access is governed by RBAC; you can create dashboards and limit token-level views to specific roles. additionally, we can redact tokens or only store aggregates if you prefer.
[05:56] Ellen Park: timeline and gating — what would you need from us to do a pilot?
[06:01] Ravi Patel: minimal: IdP metadata for SAML/SCIM, a sample network CIDR for VPC peering if Private, list of models/endpoints you'll test, and a short success criteria doc for the pilot (latency targets, cost thresholds, security gates). we'll produce a pilot checklist.
[06:18] Tara Gomez: data residency — some of our telemetry must stay in the EU. can you pin region for hosted?
[06:24] Claire Soto: yes we have region pinning on hosted for data at rest and we can route compute within specific cloud regions. for strict residency and audit controls we often recommend Dedicated in a region or Private for on-prem.
[06:36] Ben Ortiz: are there cost uplifts for KMS/HSM and private networking?
[06:40] Claire Soto: yes there are add-ons: KMS integration and HSM support have a consumption cost and setup fee for Private; network egress and dedicated capacity are part of Dedicated pricing. i'll include a pricing appendix in the follow-up.
[06:52] Marcus Li: curious about incident response — if there's a suspected data leak, what's the process? are logs immutable for forensic purposes?
[07:00] Ravi Patel: IR steps: we provide forensics logs, playbooks, and coordinate with customer SOC. logs are archived and can be exported to your SIEM; for deeper need we run forensics with your incident team under an escalation path. again, for full isolation Private is best for forensic chain-of-custody.
[07:18] Tara Gomez: audit schedule — if we want quarterly access to audit logs as auditors request, can you set automated exports?
[07:24] Claire Soto: yes, we can schedule automated exports to your S3 or SIEM with role-based access.
[07:32] Ellen Park: one more thing — do you offer field-level encryption for specific fields in the model payloads?
[07:37] Ravi Patel: we support application-level field encryption patterns. you can encrypt specific elements client-side and Redwood treats them as opaque blobs. for routing/feature flags we support tokenized references so your app can keep PII encrypted.
[07:52] Ben Ortiz: competition question — we've been talking to CloudServeAI who said they do region pinning but not full HSM support. ForgeInference claims better latency on small batches. any performance guarantees?
[08:02] Claire Soto: Redwood offers SLA-backed latency targets on Dedicated; Hosted has best-effort SLOs. performance varies with model size and sequence length — our Optimize module can recommend quantization and batching. we'll include a short benchmark that aligns to your expected workload.
[08:18] Tara Gomez: ok, wrap up and next steps please.
[08:20] Claire Soto: recap: we'll send SOC2 docs, security whitepaper, pen test summary, and a pilot checklist + sample network diagram and KMS integration notes. we'll ask you for IdP metadata, sample endpoints list, and compliance calendar. set tentative pilot kickoff for week of 2027-03-14.
[08:36] Ellen Park: thanks, that sounds good. one more ask: can you include an example RBAC policy export so we can map to our groups?
[08:42] Ravi Patel: yes, i'll drop a role to role mapping example and a minimal scim mapping template.
[08:48] Claire Soto: great. i'll follow up with links and a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff. thanks everyone.
[08:54] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings around product names (e.g., Redwood Private transcribed as "Redwood Privat" in a few spots), acronyms sometimes spaced (S O C 2), and speaker turns overlapped briefly at 00:40 and 07:50.

Shared artifacts mentioned: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2.pdf (SOC2 attestation), security-whitepaper-v2.pdf (to be shared), pilot-checklist.xlsx (to be provided), sample-network-diagram.png (to be provided).
